```{r}
# R script to reproduce happiness modeling pipeline

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(caret)
library(car)
library(ggplot2)

# --- Load dataset ---
data <- read.csv("C:/Users/coolm/Onedrive/Documents/Mental_Health_and_Social_Media_Balance_Dataset.csv")

# Use 'df' consistently
df <- data

# --- Drop ID-like columns if present 6D ---
for(n in c('User_ID','UserId','id','ID','Id','index')) {
  if(n %in% colnames(df)) {
    df <- df %>% select(-all_of(n))
  }
}

# --- Handle the target variable ---
# Check what the exact column name for happiness is
colnames(df)

# If the column is named "Happiness_Index.1.10.", use this 6A:
df$Happiness_Index.1.10.[is.na(df$Happiness_Index.1.10.)] <- mean(df$Happiness_Index.1.10., na.rm=TRUE)

# --- Set up predictors 5A---
predictors <- setdiff(colnames(df), 'Happiness_Index.1.10.')
cat_cols <- predictors[sapply(df[predictors], function(x) is.character(x) | is.factor(x))]

# --- Dummy encode categorical variables 6D ---
if(length(cat_cols) > 0) {
  dummies <- dummyVars(~ ., data = df[predictors], fullRank = TRUE)
  X <- predict(dummies, newdata = df[predictors])
} else {
  X <- as.matrix(df[predictors])
}

# --- Replace missing values in predictors 6A---
for(i in 1:ncol(X)) {
  if(any(is.na(X[,i]))) X[is.na(X[,i]), i] <- mean(X[,i], na.rm=TRUE)
}

# --- Create final model dataset 6 and 7 ---
data_model <- data.frame(happiness = df$Happiness_Index.1.10., X)

# --- Correlation matrix 5B---
cors <- cor(data_model)
write.csv(cors[,'happiness'], file='C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/corr_with_happiness_r.csv')

# --- Fit linear model 7c and 7D---
lm_full <- lm(happiness ~ ., data = data_model)
write.csv(data.frame(VIF = vif(lm_full)), file='C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/vif_happiness_r.csv')

# --- Cross-validation with caret 8B---
set.seed(42)
train_control <- trainControl(method='cv', number=10)
model <- train(happiness ~ ., data = data_model, method='lm', trControl = train_control)
print(model)

# --- Save model for later use 11---
saveRDS(model, file='C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/happiness_model_rds.rds')

```

# ================================

library(ggplot2)

    geom_boxplot() +
    labs(
      title = "Happiness by Social Media Usage Category",
      x = "Social Media Usage Level",
      y = "Happiness (1–10)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

# --- Pairwise scatterplots between numeric variables ---
numeric_df <- df %>% select(where(is.numeric))
GGally::ggpairs(
  numeric_df[, 1:min(6, ncol(numeric_df))],  # show first 6 numeric columns to keep it readable
  title = "Pairwise Relationships Between Key Variables"
)

# --- Correlation heatmap ---
corr_matrix <- cor(numeric_df, use = "complete.obs")
corrplot(
  corr_matrix,
  method = "color",
  tl.cex = 0.8,
  addCoef.col = "black",
  number.cex = 0.7,
  title = "Correlation Heatmap of Numeric Variables",
  mar = c(0,0,1,0)
)

# --- Scatterplot of Happiness vs. Screen Time (if available) ---
if("Screen_Time" %in% names(df)) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Screen_Time, y = Happiness_Index.1.10.)) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
    labs(
      title = "Relationship Between Screen Time and Happiness",
      x = "Average Daily Screen Time (hours)",
      y = "Happiness (1–10)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
# ==================================
# Part 5c: Checking Regression Assumptions
# ==================================

library(ggplot2)
library(car)
library(gridExtra)

# --- 1️⃣ Linearity & Homoscedasticity ---
# Residuals vs Fitted plot
plot(lm_full, which = 1, main = "Residuals vs Fitted")

# This plot should show random scatter around 0.
# If there’s a curve or funnel shape, it suggests non-linearity or heteroscedasticity.


# --- 2️⃣ Normality of Residuals ---
# QQ Plot
plot(lm_full, which = 2, main = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals")

# Shapiro–Wilk Test (more formal test)
shapiro.test(residuals(lm_full))

# If p-value > 0.05, residuals are approximately normal.


# --- 3️⃣ Homoscedasticity (Equal Variance) ---
# Breusch–Pagan test
car::ncvTest(lm_full)

# If p-value > 0.05, variances are roughly equal.


# --- 4️⃣ Multicollinearity ---
car::vif(lm_full)
# VIF > 5 or 10 suggests collinearity problems.


# --- 5️⃣ Influence and Leverage Diagnostics ---
# Cook’s Distance
plot(lm_full, which = 4, main = "Cook’s Distance (Influence)")

# Influence Plot
car::influencePlot(lm_full, main = "Influence Plot", id.method = "identify", sub = "Circle size ∝ Cook’s Distance")

# Observations with large Cook’s distance or leverage may be influential outliers.


# --- 6️⃣ Residual Histogram ---
res_df <- data.frame(residuals = residuals(lm_full))
ggplot(res_df, aes(x = residuals)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Model Residuals", x = "Residuals", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# --- 7️⃣ Optional: Save all diagnostic plots together ---
png("C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/happiness_regression_diagnostics.png", width = 1000, height = 800)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(lm_full)
dev.off()

```
```{r}
# ==================================
# Part 5d: Collinearity Evaluation
# ==================================

library(car)
library(caret)
library(dplyr)

# Step 1️⃣: Check Variance Inflation Factor (VIF)
vif_values <- car::vif(lm_full)
vif_table <- data.frame(Variable = names(vif_values), VIF = vif_values)
print(vif_table)

# Save to CSV for your report
write.csv(vif_table, "C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/vif_values.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Step 2️⃣: Identify problematic predictors
# (Rules of thumb: VIF > 5 indicates moderate collinearity, VIF > 10 is high)
high_vif <- vif_table %>% filter(VIF > 5)
print(high_vif)

# Step 3️⃣: If any VIFs are too high, consider removing those predictors and refitting the model
if (nrow(high_vif) > 0) {
  message("High VIF detected. Refitting model without these variables...")
  
  # Create new dataset without high-VIF predictors
  keep_vars <- setdiff(names(data_model), high_vif$Variable)
  
  # Refit the model
  lm_reduced <- lm(happiness ~ ., data = data_model[, keep_vars])
  
  # Compare models
  print(summary(lm_full)$adj.r.squared)
  print(summary(lm_reduced)$adj.r.squared)
  
  # New VIFs
  new_vif <- car::vif(lm_reduced)
  print(new_vif)
  
  # Save comparison results
  write.csv(data.frame(
    Model = c("Full", "Reduced"),
    Adj_R2 = c(summary(lm_full)$adj.r.squared, summary(lm_reduced)$adj.r.squared)
  ), "C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/model_comparison.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  
  # Save new model
  saveRDS(lm_reduced, "C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/happiness_model_reduced.rds")
}

# Step 4️⃣: Optionally visualize VIFs
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(vif_table, aes(x = reorder(Variable, VIF), y = VIF)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, color = "orange", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Variance Inflation Factors (VIF)",
       x = "Predictor Variables",
       y = "VIF Value") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/vif_plot.png", width = 8, height = 6)
```

```{r}
# ----------------------------
# 7a–7f: Modeling Section
# ----------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(car)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)

# Load dataset
df <- read.csv("C:/Users/jesge/Downloads/Mental_Health_and_Social_Media_Balance_Dataset.csv")

# Handle missing values if any
df <- df %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), mean(., na.rm = TRUE), .)))

# ----------------------------
# 7a. Univariate model exploration
# ----------------------------
# Fit simple linear regressions of Happiness_Index.1.10. on each continuous variable
continuous_vars <- c("Age", "Daily_Screen_Time.hrs.", "Sleep_Quality.1.10.", 
                     "Stress_Level.1.10.", "Days_Without_Social_Media", 
                     "Exercise_Frequency.week.")

uni_results <- lapply(continuous_vars, function(var) {
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste("Happiness_Index.1.10. ~", var)), data = df)
  summary(model)$coefficients[2, c("Estimate", "Pr(>|t|)")]
})
names(uni_results) <- continuous_vars
uni_results

# ----------------------------
# 7b. Interaction and confounding exploration
# ----------------------------
# Check a few potential interactions (e.g., Stress × Sleep, ScreenTime × Exercise)
interaction_model <- lm(Happiness_Index.1.10. ~ Stress_Level.1.10. * Sleep_Quality.1.10. + 
                          Daily_Screen_Time.hrs. * Exercise_Frequency.week. + 
                          Age + Gender + Days_Without_Social_Media + Social_Media_Platform, data = df)
summary(interaction_model)

# ----------------------------
# 7c. Comprehensive model
# ----------------------------
lm_full <- lm(Happiness_Index.1.10. ~ ., data = df)
summary(lm_full)

# ----------------------------
# 7d. Simplified stepwise regression with a smaller starting model
lm_start <- lm(Happiness_Index.1.10. ~ Sleep_Quality.1.10. + 
                 Stress_Level.1.10. + 
                 Daily_Screen_Time.hrs. + 
                 Exercise_Frequency.week. + 
                 Days_Without_Social_Media,
               data = df)

step_model <- step(lm_start, direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_model)

# ----------------------------
# 7e. Model Diagnostics (Regression Assumptions)

# 1. Linearity — plot residuals vs fitted values
plot(step_model$fitted.values, resid(step_model),
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted (Linearity Check)",
     xlab = "Fitted Values", ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

# 2. Normality of residuals — Q-Q plot + Shapiro-Wilk test
qqnorm(resid(step_model))
qqline(resid(step_model), col = "red")
shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(resid(step_model))
print(shapiro_test)

# 3. Homoscedasticity (equal variance) — Breusch-Pagan test
library(lmtest)
bp_test <- bptest(step_model)
print(bp_test)

# 4. Independence of errors — Durbin-Watson test
library(car)
dw_test <- durbinWatsonTest(step_model)
print(dw_test)

# ----------------------------
# 7f. Final best model
# ----------------------------
summary(step_model)

# Save final model if needed
saveRDS(step_model, "final_happiness_model.rds")

```
